items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: But we used to joke about it. It became a thing. He was a fantastic man.

ctx.x: You were telling me that during your long friendship with Strayhorn you repeatedly asked him for just eight bars?

Oh, yeah. I kept saying to him, you know, I said, "How about writing me an arrangement?" And he would say, "No, I really can't." And I would say, "Well, look, just eight bars. How about eight bars and we'll build a whole thing on it," and I never did get the eight bars. But we used to joke about it. It became a thing. He was a fantastic man. He -- I can't think of any greater complement to Duke than his finding Billy Strayhorn, because it was such a wonderful mixture. Billy Strayhorn gave a delicacy to the…

couldn't have found anybody to interpret what he was doing -- well, you get back to the old thing, the alter ego, the association there. You couldn't tell where one left off and the other started, and without each other -- well, let's put it this way. I doubt very much if we'd have heard much about Billy if he hadn't gotten associated with Duke, because he was too subtle in a very rough world of music. Of course I think if I could have found him I might have been able to do something, but on the other hand where…
